Mercurii / The shiftSource: Allium, State of Stablecoins and Payments, Sep 202602 / 09

Start wide. Allium estimates $401–527 billion in stablecoin payments from January to August 2026, including $137–153 billion B2B, with 58–64% of volume received by businesses. These are third-party multi-chain volume estimates, not Mercurii's traction and not our revenue TAM.

The shift is from pure transfer rails toward business use. A business now needs the systems around the payment.

MercuriiProblem
02 — Problem

A public wallet makes company
finance an open book.

What becomes visible

A linked public treasury can reveal who gets paid, when, and how your business moves.

A transfer is not a financial operating system.

Mercurii / ProblemPrivacy boundary: Solana documentation · company-workflow framing is our product thesis03 / 09

Do not claim all business users experience this to the same degree; this is a specific pain hypothesis for stablecoin-operating teams. Public-chain transaction and account data can reveal balances, counterparties, timing and payment patterns. Separately, a company needs explicit roles, approvals and records rather than a shared wallet. We will validate the severity with design partners.

Mercurii / Target marketBuyer count, willingness to pay and revenue TAM are under validation · no customer interviews claimed06 / 09

Our narrow starting customer is a small stablecoin studio, crypto agency or startup that already receives stablecoins and repeatedly pays remote contractors or vendors. Finance is often founder-led, and the team experiences both privacy and approval pain.

This is a beachhead hypothesis, not a measured customer cohort. We have no interviews, qualified-account count or willingness-to-pay evidence yet, so do not present the broad stablecoin payment volume as Mercurii's TAM.

Mercurii / InsightMercurii product thesis · not yet a proven competitive moat04 / 09

This is our distinctive insight, not a market statistic. A private payment can still leave a company juggling approvals, roles and records elsewhere. Our hypothesis is that confidential operating state and enforceable business authority, delivered as one workflow, are more valuable to the first customer than privacy of a single transfer alone. Competitors cover parts of this space; we need user evidence to prove differentiation.

Mercurii / ProductProduct design and repository implementation · current end-to-end browser flow remains to be revalidated05 / 09

Walk through the operating loop: receive, approve, pay and reconcile. The intended roles are Founder, Finance, Manager and Employee. Agents can read only scoped information and draft unsigned treasury requests; they do not get unlimited authority to spend. A separately capped x402 float is a different bounded flow. The product experience is under active integration; do not claim the full browser flow is currently production-ready.

MagicBlock PER

TEE-backed private execution and scoped access for delegated company state.

eSPL private token flow+ER-local permissions+Mercurii role policy
Mercurii / ArchitectureMagicBlock PER docs · Solana privacy boundary07 / 09

Why MagicBlock? A standard public Solana account cannot keep the company's internal operating state private. MagicBlock's Private Ephemeral Rollup gives delegated state permissioned access and private execution on a TEE-backed validator. Mercurii layers business-role policy on top; eSPL supports the private token path. We are not using PER as a synonym for generic private payments or claiming total anonymity.

Important boundary for questions: base-layer entry and exit, account shells, timing and network metadata can still be observable. PER visibility does not replace application authorization; the program must enforce roles and limits. Private state must not be committed as plaintext. See the repository security notes.

MercuriiPrivate Financial Operations09 / 09

End on the world we want, not a product feature list. If companies are going to operate with stablecoins, they need the same confidentiality and separation of duties that serious finance teams expect, while keeping noncustodial access to open settlement rails. Our immediate ask is design partners: teams paying people or vendors in stablecoins who will help validate and test the workflow.
